knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The colour does not protect anything by itself. Keeping each colour in its area, and not swapping cloths during the job, is what prevents transfer.
Colour meanings are set by each business. The worker confirms the key before setting up rather than assuming it.
A dropped cloth is taken out of use, the affected surface is re-cleaned with an assigned cloth, and the event is recorded and reported.

practicalCriteria: Confirms the colour key or cloth-to-area mapping before setup and records it on the job sheet, observed by the assessor.
Keeps cloth and tool sets apart in the kit; no cross-use is observed during a simulated multi-area clean.
Removes a deliberately crossed cloth from use, re-cleans the affected surface with an assigned cloth, and records the event.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. Practical competence: assessor sign-off against each practical criterion, with no uncorrected cross-area transfer during the simulated clean. A knowledge-check pass does not verify practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation sheet for the simulated multi-area clean
Cross-area event record for the deliberate correction
stopWorkCriteria: A cloth is used across areas without correction
The worker proceeds on an assumed colour key without confirmation
